questions.prompt: Where does the JMeter HTTP(S) Test Script Recorder sit during recording?
options: As a proxy between the browser and the application
As a browser extension that reads the DOM
questions.explanation: The recorder is an HTTP(S) proxy; the browser sends traffic through it and JMeter turns requests into samplers.

questions.prompt: Which template gives you a ready-made plan with a recorder and Recording Controller?
questions.explanation: The built-in Recording template sets up the recorder, a Thread Group with a Recording Controller and useful defaults.

questions.prompt: To record HTTPS sites, the browser must trust JMeter's generated root CA certificate.
questions.explanation: JMeter performs a man-in-the-middle on TLS to see requests, so the browser must trust ApacheJMeterTemporaryRootCA.

questions.prompt: Your recording contains hundreds of requests to .png, .css, .js and analytics domains. What is the best way to keep the script focused?
options: Use 'URL Patterns to Exclude' (e.g. the 'Add suggested Excludes' button) and exclude third-party hosts
Set the Thread Group to 1 thread
questions.explanation: Exclude patterns stop static and third-party requests from becoming samplers; you can model static resources separately if needed. The other options do not filter requests.

questions.prompt: Which setting groups recorded requests per page/user action so the plan is readable?
options: Grouping: 'Put each group in a new Transaction Controller' (with a pause between groups)
questions.explanation: Grouping uses idle gaps between requests to split actions into controllers. The others do not group requests.

questions.prompt: Which are typical clean-up steps after recording? Select all that apply.
options: Correlate dynamic values such as session ids and CSRF tokens
Add assertions to check real success
Keep hard-coded recorded tokens so the replay matches exactly
questions.explanation: Recorded tokens expire and are user-specific, so they must be extracted at run time. Data and assertions make the script realistic and trustworthy.

questions.prompt: Recording works for HTTP pages but HTTPS pages fail in the browser with a certificate error, even after importing the CA last month. What is the most likely reason?
options: The generated CA certificate has a limited validity (7 days by default) and was regenerated; import the new ApacheJMeterTemporaryRootCA.crt from bin
HTTPS recording requires JMeter in non-GUI mode
questions.explanation: JMeter's temporary root CA is valid for a limited time (7 days by default) and is recreated, so the browser trusts an outdated one. Non-GUI mode, disabling JS or using port 443 do not fix trust.

questions.prompt: A recorded login works once, but under 20 users every login after the first few returns 'invalid request'. The recorded POST contains `execution=e1s1&_eventId=submit&lt=LT-123-abc`. What is needed?
options: Extract the lt/execution values from the login page response for each user and substitute them, because they are one-time tokens
Add a Constant Timer of 5 seconds
questions.explanation: Login flows (such as CAS-style forms) issue per-session tokens that must be correlated. Timers, method changes or heap size do not make an expired token valid.

coding.title: Apply recorder exclude patterns
coding.prompt:
The recorder's 'URL Patterns to Exclude' are regular expressions that must match the **whole** URL. Write `kept(urls, excludes)` returning the URLs that match none of the patterns (use `re.fullmatch`), in original order.

Example: with excludes `[r'.*\.(png|css|js)', r'https?://[^/]*google-analytics\.com/.*']`, `http://shop/app.js` is dropped and `http://shop/cart` is kept.
coding.explanation: JMeter applies recorder patterns to the whole URL, which is why suggested excludes start with `.*`. A pattern like `\.png` alone would match nothing.
hints: Keep a URL only if no pattern matches.
`[u for u in urls if not any(re.fullmatch(p, u) for p in excludes)]`

coding.title: Spot values that need correlation
coding.prompt:
Compare two recordings of the same journey. Write `dynamic_params(rec1, rec2)` where each recording is a list of query/body strings like `'user=bob&token=ab12'`, one per request in the same order. Return a sorted list of parameter names whose value differs between the two recordings for the same request.

Example: `['a=1&t=x'], ['a=1&t=y']` returns `['t']`.
coding.explanation: Recording a journey twice and diffing is a standard way to find session ids and tokens: anything that changes between identical journeys is a correlation candidate.
hints: Compare the dicts key by key (include keys present in only one).
Collect differing names in a set and return it sorted.
